class.name: SchemaColumn
class.description: Declaration order is address order, so a column's index in [member SchemaRecord.columns] is what every binding addresses it by and, for a table, the position its bytes occupy in a frame. [br][br]A column is declaration and no storage. The value shape it names decides which storage array a [TableCore] fills for it, which [method SchemaCore.storage_type] answers, and which [enum Variant.Type] one of its elements reads as, which [method SchemaCore.element_type] answers. [codeblock] var column := SchemaColumn.create(&"cooldown", SchemaCore.ColumnType.F32, 8) column.quantizer = NetwQuantizeFixed.new().step(0.01) [/codeblock]

method.name: create
method.description: Returns a column named [param key] holding [param type], where one row occupies [param stride] elements. [br][br]A registered class takes no constructor arguments, so this is the three-value form [method SchemaCore.append_column] builds columns through. Prefer that verb, which also refuses a duplicate key and honours the seal.

members.member: The caller-facing name, unique within its schema and part of the shape hash [method SchemaCore.compute_hash] folds.

The bit packer this column's elements cross the wire through, or [code]null[/code] for the raw little-endian memcpy path. Never consulted at rest, because saves are unquantized. [br][br]Part of the shape, so two peers that packed the same column to different bit widths disagree at [method SchemaCore.hash_of] rather than misreading every later frame. Assign it before the seal through [method SchemaCore.assign_quantizer], which refuses once the declaration is fixed.
How many elements one row occupies. A fixed-capacity array is expressed as a stride rather than as a second type family, so eight ability cooldowns is one [PackedFloat32Array] of stride eight.
The value shape, one of [enum SchemaCore.ColumnType].
